title: How he found bands at parties; Celestin's second band
summary: Friends took him to varied places, including a Stuart Bergen dance and a medical fraternity party where Celestin's second band played; Allen explains the second band's off-Bourbon jobs.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: I don't, no, I don't think it was one of them. I expect it might come to me, but I don't remember. I know what would happen, you know, would be somebody would, sometimes you, sometimes Bob Greenwood, sometimes, I think I went to several places with Joan Whitehead when she was in New Orleans. Various people would get in touch and say, you know, what's his name is playing out at such and such a place, let's go. And sometimes I'd say, we'll be able to get in, and they'd say, oh sure, the musicians will say it's okay. And sometimes I had my doubts. For example, we went to the, and I don't remember who was in this particular business, went to the Audubon Tea Room for a fraternity dance that none of us had any connection with when Stuart Bergen's band was playing. And no one seemed to raise any questions. I went to a variety of places this way. Of course, you know, it was even, it, the time that I, that I particularly listened a lot to Celestan's second band turned out to be a party that the medical school fraternity I belonged to was giving. In fact, out at the New Orleans Country Club. And I had no idea who the band was going to be. And I don't guess I was particularly interested because at the time I didn't expect much. And we went out there and, much to my surprise and delight, in comes this jazz band. And they were great. And it was real fun. I suspect, perhaps, if I had known, I would have, I would have taken a camera. But I had a date and didn't know anything about it in advance. I was what I would suspect I would call nowadays incredibly naive about what did go on. But then I was naive about a lot of things at the time.

Well, yeah. And, well, and the thing is, the fact is, almost nobody knew about what was going on. As I was saying, much of it was private parties. And things, and Celestan even had a number two band, you mentioned. Yeah. And that was really for playing jobs away from Bourbon Street. He somehow managed to get off. And I would run into them coming out of, say, the St. Charles Hotel. I can remember that one day. And talking to them.
